audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers tell you that Public Execution 'suppresses through his passive immunity' — in whys[4], in spikes[1].text and again in breakdown mid. Riot's text for Goes Where He Pleases says the opposite.
audit.why: Riot: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby.' Public Execution's suppress-and-stun is an immobilising effect, so the page is promising a player that their 130s ultimate pierces the one mechanic built to eat it. Baiting the cannister out first is correct whichever way that specific interaction resolves; telling them it goes through is not.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1].text and phases[4].why now say to bait the passive out before spending R, and no longer claim the suppress ignores it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper is described only as 'his W regen' and 'sustain + reset'. The condition on its healing — the whole counterplay — is stated nowhere.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'At the end of the duration or on Recast, Dr. Mundo deals a burst of damage to nearby enemies. If the burst hit an enemy, he heals a percentage of the stored damage.' No hit, no heal. Heart Zapper is 325 range on a 17s cooldown, so a melee champion with three dashes can bank her damage and simply not be there when it detonates — which turns his best sustain tool into a wasted 17 seconds.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, report[5].t and wants.foe[1] now state that the burst must connect for him to heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', and Levels 4-5 was the generic 'lane-control window' template while the content layer calls that stage Ambessa's weakest.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is her only shield. At 4-5 her Q sits at 14-11s and E at 13-10s against a 4s Infected Bonesaw and a 16s Heart Zapper, so he simply out-cycles her.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why now carries the Heart Zapper condition and phases[3].why the real cooldown mismatch.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain', and Maximum Dosage's cooldown appears nowhere in either layer.
audit.why: Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s at every rank against Public Execution's 130s, and it heals a percentage of MISSING health instantly before regenerating more over a long duration. Burning him to 20% and then failing to finish is the worst possible outcome, because that is precisely when his ultimate pays the most.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and dontsFull[2].d now name the 120s cooldown and the missing-health scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blunt Force Trauma is never named in either layer, so nothing on the page tells you what his melee burst looks like.
audit.why: Riot's text: it is an on-next-attack strike dealing additional damage based on his MISSING health, on 9s at rank 1 down to 6s. It is an attack reset, so the tell is the wind-up, and it hits hardest exactly when he is low — the moment Ambessa is most tempted to stay in for the kill.
audit.corrected: Recorded here; I did not have a field to place it in without cutting something more load-bearing, and the applier would reject an over-length rewrite.

notes: The claim I removed matters more than the ones I added: both layers stated that Public Execution 'suppresses through his passive immunity', and Riot's own Goes Where He Pleases text is 'resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him'. Whether Ambessa's suppression is a special case is not settled anywhere in the data — needsResearch is empty on her file — so I rewrote the advice to 'bait the cannister out first', which is correct either way, and marked that audit entry Medium confidence. Please verify the suppression-versus-passive interaction before shipping. Content also repeatedly credits Ambessa's R with 'ability-hit healing'; her kit file carries a heal flag on R but Riot's description of Public Execution says nothing about healing, so I neither repeated nor deleted that claim. Blunt Force Trauma (9s to 6s, attack reset, damage scaling with HIS missing health) is named nowhere in this matchup and deserves a field.
